n: Hủ Tiếu Hồ Đỗ Khiêm (Đinh Hòa)
address: 26 Đinh Hòa, Ward 13, District 8, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 60-plus-year, second-generation Teochew (Triều Châu) shop on Đinh Hòa run by the Đỗ family — the reference address in Saigon for hủ tiếu hồ, a near-vanished Chaozhou dish of thin square rice sheets in a clear sweet broth served only with braised pork offal and pickled mustard greens. Busy from morning, especially weekends.
dish: hủ tiếu hồ (Teochew rice-sheet noodles with braised pork offal)

n: Bún Chua Cay Macao (Suan La Fen)
address: 51 Bửu Đình, Ward 5, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) family stall in a Bửu Đình alley just west of Chợ Lớn serving suan la fen — a fiery, tongue-numbing hot-and-sour noodle rooted in Chongqing, built on black vinegar and satay with dozens of toppings (spare rib, frog, beef ball, seafood) and a century-egg-in-soy starter. Order the chili level; three grades from mild to very hot.
dish: bún chua cay Macao / suan la fen (hot-and-sour noodles)

address: 200 Lê Quang Sung, Ward 2, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 40-year Hoa dessert counter on Lê Quang Sung by Bình Tây Market, cited as District 6's most famous chè shop — heaped bowls of Chinese herbal sweet soups (chè phục linh, sâm bổ lượng) loaded with longan, lotus seed, seaweed jelly and coconut. A Chợ Lớn-west institution for chè Tàu.
dish: chè Tàu / Chinese herbal sweet soups (phục linh, sâm bổ lượng)

n: Bánh Hẹ Lê Quang Sung (Khu Người Hoa)
address: Lê Quang Sung, Ward 2, District 6, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 70-year Teochew snack stall on Lê Quang Sung, in the Hoa quarter around Bình Tây / Phùng Hưng markets, that has drawn generations for bánh hẹ — pan-fried garlic-chive cakes of rice flour and hẹ — alongside taro and jicama versions. One of the last strongholds of a Chợ Lớn street snack.
dish: bánh hẹ (Teochew pan-fried garlic-chive rice cakes)
